READING

**The loan-term constraint is the load-bearing fact**

The bank wrote on 2026-06-22 that a licence term shorter than the loan (2039) would put the facility under review. That is not a vague warning; it is a stated bank position in writing. A fifteen-year renewal from 2028 runs to ~2043, comfortably clear of 2039. A six-year renewal from 2028 runs to ~2034, five years short of loan maturity and squarely inside the bank's concern.

The precedent for the undertaking route is unambiguous and consistent: Cadgarth (2024) and Nant Elwy (2025) both filed with undertakings and both received six years, not fifteen. The problem presents this as the Board's practice, not an aberration. There is no basis in the facts to expect Blaenclydach to receive fifteen years via an undertaking when two comparable schemes did not. The Board evidently treats the undertaking as a reduced-confidence filing and calibrates the term accordingly.

PENNYQUAY therefore does not merely produce a slightly shorter licence; it reliably produces a licence term the bank has already said triggers a review of a GBP 480,000 facility. For a two-person operation, a bank review is existential: potential loan recall, forced renegotiation, additional security demands. The GBP 8,436 outage saving is trivially small against that exposure. PENNYQUAY's apparent cheapness is not economy; it is a hidden catastrophic liability.

---

**The derogation probability is higher than the raw 4/11 ratio implies**

The Board decided eleven applications in 2025 in fourteen weeks. Four were granted, seven refused. The critical published fact is that every refusal named a scheme with no dated regulatory driver. This is the Board's own stated reason for refusal. It means the 7/11 refusal rate applies to a population that includes schemes without a regulatory hook — schemes that, on the Board's logic, should not have applied. Blaenclydach has a precisely dated and non-discretionary regulatory driver: the abstraction licence renewal must be lodged by 2027-05-31, that renewal requires a fish-pass compliance certificate, and only the replacement screen can produce one. The chain is locked and dated to the day.

On the published pattern, schemes with dated drivers were granted; schemes without were refused. Blaenclydach fits the profile of a grant. I would put the probability of approval at 75–85%, not the base-rate 36%. The GBP 9,000 application fee is a reasonable premium to access that probability.

---

**Timing check for LINTHAUGH**

Derogation lodged 2026-10-19. Decision 2027-01-25 — fourteen weeks, consistent with the Board's own 2025 pace. February works commence immediately after grant; six weeks of in-river works puts commissioning around mid-March 2027. Certificate follows within six weeks: ready by late April / early May 2027. Renewal lodged before 2027-05-31. ✓ The chain is tight but it closes.

---

**Full cost comparison**

*LINTHAUGH, granted (high probability):*
GBP 9,000 (application) + GBP 46,000 (deposit, applied to contract) + GBP 19,152 (winter export loss) = **GBP 74,152**
Outcome: complete renewal file, fifteen-year licence, loan secure, bank satisfied.

*LINTHAUGH, refused (low probability):*
GBP 9,000 + GBP 46,000 (deposit, irrecoverable) = GBP 55,000 sunk, then fallback to July undertaking route (GBP 8,436) = **GBP 63,436 total**
Outcome: six-year renewal, bank review — identical to PENNYQUAY but GBP 55,000 more expensive. This is the downside, not the expected case.

*PENNYQUAY:*
GBP 8,436 (July outage). Outcome: six-year renewal, bank review — certain, not probabilistic.

Expected cost of LINTHAUGH is approximately GBP 74,152 × 0.80 + GBP 63,436 × 0.20 ≈ GBP 72,008. Against this the only material saving from PENNYQUAY is the difference between GBP 72,008 and GBP 8,436 — roughly GBP 63,500 — but that difference buys certainty of a bank review rather than avoidance of one. The trade is unfavourable by any reasonable weighting of the bank risk.

---

**The deposit risk in context**

GBP 46,000 is committed on 2026-12-01, five weeks before the 2027-01-25 decision. In a refusal scenario it is gone. That is real money — roughly 10% of the annual export revenue at current tariffs. But it only becomes an irrecoverable loss when combined with a refusal, which is the lower-probability outcome. And even in that scenario the scheme is still operating; the bank-facility problem is the same as under PENNYQUAY, not worse. The deposit risk is the price of buying a good-probability route to a fifteen-year term. That price is worth paying.

---

**Summary**

PENNYQUAY produces the same bank-facility risk as the worst case of LINTHAUGH, but it does so with certainty and forecloses the path to a fifteen-year term entirely. LINTHAUGH, at materially higher upfront cost, carries a high-probability route to the renewal term that keeps the loan facility intact. The GBP 65,000-odd cost difference is not extravagance; it is the premium on removing the existential bank risk that PENNYQUAY guarantees.

---

READING
PENNYQUAY's apparent economy is illusory because the undertaking route consistently delivers six-year renewals (per Cadgarth and Nant Elwy), producing a licence term shorter than the 2039 loan maturity and triggering the bank review the bank has already flagged in writing. LINTHAUGH carries a high probability of approval given Blaenclydach's precisely dated regulatory driver, which matches the profile of every granted application in the Board's 2025 record. The timing chain works — derogation decided 2027-01-25, works complete mid-March, certificate by late April, renewal filed complete before 2027-05-31 — delivering a fifteen-year licence that clears the loan term. Even the worst-case refusal scenario under LINTHAUGH leaves the scheme operational, merely replicating PENNYQUAY's outcome at GBP 55,000 additional cost; the expected outcome under LINTHAUGH is a secure fifteen-year renewal. The GBP 74,152 expected cost of LINTHAUGH is the price of avoiding a bank review of a GBP 480,000 facility, and that price is worth paying. PENNYQUAY is not the cheap course; it is the course that trades a modest outage saving for a near-certain bank review, which for a two-person scheme is an existential risk.

CALL
LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
PENNYQUAY reliably delivers a six-year renewal via the undertaking route — as Cadgarth and Nant Elwy prove — which falls short of the 2039 loan maturity and triggers the bank review the bank has already signalled, while LINTHAUGH's precisely dated regulatory driver fits the Board's own published grant profile and offers a high-probability route to a fifteen-year renewal that keeps the facility secure.
